taskDescription: Click each word that names one of the four downstream pathways activated when mitochondrial superoxide inhibits GAPDH in hyperglycaemia.
textField: When mitochondrial superoxide activates PARP and inhibits GAPDH, glycolytic intermediates above GAPDH are diverted into four damaging pathways: the *polyol* pathway, which depletes NADPH and accumulates sorbitol; the *AGE* pathway, which cross-links proteins through non-enzymatic glycation; the *PKC* pathway, which alters vascular permeability and blood flow; and the *hexosamine* pathway, which modifies transcription factors by O-linked glycosylation.

overallFeedback.feedback: The four pathways — polyol, AGE, PKC and hexosamine — all branch from the same upstream event: mitochondrial overproduction of superoxide inhibiting GAPDH. This unifying mechanism explains why tight glucose control reduces all microvascular complications and why targeting a single downstream pathway has limited benefit.
